cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Give It Up
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender something they value.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Let me have the medal for the charity auction.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the only thing I've ever won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Then it should raise more than the toaster.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I lend it for the display? I still want people to know I won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then present it to the buyer yourself. I'll print your name in the programme; everyone will know whose medal was worth giving up.

mechanism: A grants a medal owner ceremonial recognition in exchange for surrendering the valued medal, assuming power to approve the terms.
confusable: Simply confiscating an object is not persuasion; B attachment must shape an appealing concession A offers from above.
comparison: Public recognition is traded for a medal; the guitar alternative preserves a private keepsake while seeking household funds.
seedUse: D12-a supplies the only medal and display compromise; S01 makes a recognition concession into a granted honor.
